snip.t: Thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) is a coenzyme derived from vitamin B1 (thiamine).
(b) Thiamine (as thiamine pyrophosphate, TPP) is an essential cofactor for pyruvate dehydrogenase and α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase (and transketolase).
Objective biochemical tests of thiamine status include measurement of erythrocyte transketolase activity and the thiamine pyrophosphate effect.

qs.q: A patient with a history of alcohol abuse presents with confusion, ataxia, and ophthalmoplegia. Administration of thiamine (vitamin B1) is crucial. Which of the following enzymes, critical for carbohydrate metabolism, is directly dependent on thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) as a cofactor?
qs.e: The pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, crucial for converting pyruvate to acetyl-CoA, requires thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP) as a cofactor.

qs.q: A patient with chronic alcoholism presents with neurological symptoms due to Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, caused by a deficiency in thiamine pyrophosphate. Which key metabolic multi-enzyme complex is directly impaired?
o: Glycogen phosphorylase complex regulating hepatic glycogenolysis breakdown rates
ATP synthase rotary complex generating cellular energy across membranes
Carbamoyl phosphate synthetase initiating urea synthesis inside liver cells
Glucose 6 phosphate dehydrogenase controlling pentose phosphate pathway flux
Pyruvate dehydrogenase complex linking glycolysis pathways to citric acid cycles
qs.e: Thiamine pyrophosphate is an essential coenzyme for the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex, alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase, and transketolase.
